svg.aria-label: Practical roles for men and boys who want to be allies, by relationship. A father shares the care work, pays the fees before anything else, and refuses a marriage offer out loud. A partner treats her income and her decisions as hers. A brother does his share of the housework and does not repeat what is said about a girl at school. A male teacher states the school's re-entry position and never identifies a returning mother. A faith leader says from the front that shame belongs to no girl, and asks about the responsibility of adult men. A local official makes the by-laws known and ensures one person owns a case. The test in every case is whether a girl is safer, freer and more able to choose.
svg.text: What an ally actually does
Not a statement of support. A change in conduct, by relationship.
A FATHER
Shares the care work rather than supervising it. Pays her fees
before the discretionary spending. Refuses a marriage offer out loud.
A PARTNER
Treats her income as hers and her decisions as hers. Does not
require an account of where she has been.
A BROTHER
Does his share of the housework, so her study time is not the
household’s spare capacity. Does not repeat what is said about a girl.
A TEACHER
States the school’s re-entry position before anyone asks. Never
identifies a returning mother. Treats clinic visits as legitimate.
A FAITH LEADER
Says from the front that shame belongs to no girl. Asks openly
about the responsibility of adult men. Will not bless an under-age union.
AN OFFICIAL
Makes the by-laws known in a form people read. Ensures one person
owns a case from referral to resolution.
THE TEST, IN EVERY CASE
Is she safer, freer, and more able to choose her own future than she was before?
If the honest answer is no, it was not allyship. It was a new person deciding for her.
Treasured Vessels Girls’ Centre · treasuredvesselsuganda.org
